title: Weak Cryptography and Deprecated Hash Functions
platform_conditions: PHP 7.4/8.x; password_hash (bcrypt/argon2) and random_bytes (CSPRNG) are available, md5/sha1 remain fast general-purpose hashes often misapplied to passwords
security_mechanism: md5 and sha1 are unsalted and designed to be fast: after any leak of the stored digests, offline guessing runs at GPU speeds, so password digests computed with them fall to bulk cracking. password_hash applies bcrypt/argon2 with a per-hash salt and a cost factor that makes verification deliberately slow, which is what makes storage resistant. rand(), mt_rand() and uniqid() (microsecond time plus a small constant component by default) are predictable — mt_range state is recoverable from observed outputs — so tokens and reset codes drawn from them are guessable; random_bytes() draws from the CSPRNG. Comparing digests with == short-circuits at the first differing byte and leaks a timing oracle that recovers authenticators byte by byte.

source_sink_clues.source: Credential and token material itself: password values, session/reset tokens, API keys, MAC tags generated or compared by the application.
source_sink_clues.sink: md5/sha1 applied to passwords; rand/mt_rand/uniqid feeding security tokens; == / != comparisons of digests or MACs; missing session_regenerate_id() after authentication state changes

tracking_guards: Require password_hash + password_verify for credentials; require random_bytes for any security token; require hash_equals for authenticator comparison; require session_regenerate_id(true) at login and privilege escalation points.
not_candidate_when: The fast hash digests non-secret content (file checksums, cache keys), the PRNG output feeds non-security features such as sampling or nonces for display, or the session ID is already regenerated at every privilege transition.
public_references: CWE-327: Use of a Broken or Risky Cryptographic Algorithm — https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/327.html
CWE-338: Use of Cryptographically Weak Pseudo-Random Number Generator — https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/338.html
